BuildId.description: build id (`bld-…`); must belong to the template
BuildId.name: build_id

IdempotencyKey.description: Optional exactly-once key for this create: send your own opaque, key-unique value (a UUID) to make the call safe to retry after a lost response (network timeout, 5xx). The first request creates the sandbox and ties it to the key; every later request with the same account key, Idempotency-Key and request body returns that same sandbox instead of a second, billable one. Ties are retained 24 h (GATEWAY_IDEMPOTENCY_RETENTION_S); a concurrent or early retry while the first create is still in flight returns 409 idempotency_in_progress (retry shortly, same key); reusing a key with a different body returns 409 idempotency_key_reused; a create that fails before the sandbox exists releases the key immediately so a retry can create. Omit the header to keep the default (non-idempotent) behavior.
IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

A fork inherits the source sandbox's size: cpuCount/memoryMB/diskSizeMB/resourceClass are a 400 here too unless the deployment's upstream honors per-request sizing; timeout (SANDBOX_MAX_TIMEOUT_S) and network validation are applied exactly like a create. EGRESS_POLICY_ENABLED deployments: the network block may carry networkOff (translated like a create) and a body without allowOut/denyOut inherits the source's stored lists per side (an explicit internet allow in the body speaks for itself and inherits nothing; paired with an explicit deny-all it is a 400, as on create)

allowInternetAccess.description: camelCase twin of allow_internet_access; both accepted

cpuCount.description: refused — a fork inherits the source sandbox's size (forwarded bounded by TEMPLATE_MAX_CPU only when the deployment's upstream honors per-request sizing)

diskSizeMB.description: refused — a fork inherits the source sandbox's size (forwarded bounded by TEMPLATE_MAX_DISK_MB only when the deployment's upstream honors per-request sizing)

memoryMB.description: refused — a fork inherits the source sandbox's size (forwarded bounded by TEMPLATE_MAX_MEMORY_MB only when the deployment's upstream honors per-request sizing)

network.description: {allowOut?, denyOut?} egress policy — validated and canonicalised like PUT /sandboxes/{id}/network (see NetworkUpdate); under EGRESS_POLICY_ENABLED the block may also carry networkOff, and an explicit internet allow beside the canonical deny-all is a 400 (the pair has no single meaning)

resourceClass.description: refused — a fork inherits the source sandbox's size (forwarded only when the deployment's upstream honors per-request sizing)

timeout.description: keep-alive seconds; capped at the node's SANDBOX_MAX_TIMEOUT_S A key with its own max_timeout_s cap (set by the operator) is clamped to min(SANDBOX_MAX_TIMEOUT_S, that cap) instead of getting a 400, and the response reports the applied value in X-Sandbox-Timeout-Applied.

GpuAccel.description: GPU lease request, flag-gated (the key needs a GPU grant or GPU-enabled tier; 403 without, 402 with an empty GPU bucket). A free-tier key is limited to its trial: by default a slice over 2 GiB, `network: internet`, a class other than nvidia.5090, a `template` other than the default or an `idle_timeout_s` of 0 or over 600 s is a 403 with error_code `gpu_free_tier_limit` (the body's `param` names the field), and the message says how to lift it. A body carrying `accel` creates a GPU lease (`gl-*` id, 201 -> {sandboxID, templateID, phase, accel}) instead of a CPU sandbox; the CPU fields above do not apply to it. Drive the lease with POST /sandboxes/{id}/exec ({code, timeout_s}), POST .../pause, POST .../resume, GET .../files, DELETE /sandboxes/{id}. A lease is killed by a timeout_s overrun, a VRAM over-cap kill, a dead worker or the maximum lease age. See https://sbx.agent-next.com/docs/.

class.description: GPU class to place the lease on: one the fleet serves now (GET /v0/gpu/capacity lists them, e.g. nvidia.5090). The lease lands only on a node that lists it, and the reply, GET and list report that class. A class nothing serves -> 400 `gpu_class_unavailable` with the available ones, nothing placed; while a node did not answer (it may serve the class) -> retryable 503 `gpu_node_unreachable`. A class the operator rents on demand that no node serves yet -> retryable 503 `gpu_class_provisioning` (Retry-After and `eta_s` are the seconds until a node should take leases), or 503 `gpu_class_no_supply` when the provider reported no stock (Retry-After 300, `alternatives` lists the classes served now). Omitted -> any node with a seat, and the reply names the class the lease got

reserve.description: hard-cap hosts only: what the worker does with its slice reserve between jobs. `exec` (default, for every template) hands the full slice to the job's own allocator; `hold` (an explicit opt-in) keeps it for the whole lease

template.description: operator-allowlisted worker image name; an unknown name -> 400 listing the valid ones (discover with GET /gpu/templates). Never an image reference

tier.description: fixed slice size: S 1, M 2, L 8, XL 32 GiB; an alternative to vram_gb (both given must agree, else 400). Nothing above the card's max_admit_gib (GET /v0/gpu/capacity) is admitted, so XL is not seatable on today's card

vram_gb.description: VRAM slice in GiB, enforced as a hard cap; out of range or non-numeric -> 400

wait_s.description: opt-in server-side wait for a GPU seat. 0 (default) refuses at once when the plane is full. With wait_s > 0 the create waits up to that many seconds (idle residents are suspended for the waiter) and returns 201 as soon as a seat is admitted, or the same typed `gpu_capacity_exhausted` refusal with Retry-After when the wait expires. A class rented on demand (`gpu_class_provisioning`) is waited for the same way; `gpu_class_no_supply` returns at once. Lease-cap, credit and fair-share refusals return at once. Outside [0, 120] -> 400

ListedSandbox.description: Sandbox minus the credential fields: envdAccessToken and trafficAccessToken are always stripped on bulk surfaces

NetworkPolicy.description: GET /sandboxes/{id}/network's read-back of the stored egress policy (EGRESS_POLICY_ENABLED). No stored policy answers `{}`; otherwise both lists are the canonical entries the gateway last forwarded (empty list = that side was cleared) and `source` names the view's owner — the gateway's stored record, which an out-of-band upstream mutation could diverge from

allowOut.description: canonical allowOut entries (egress.py normalisation: CIDR/IP/hostname, presets already expanded)

source.description: whose view of the policy this is: the gateway's stored record, not a live upstream read

NetworkUpdate.description: {allowOut?, denyOut?, networkOff?}; an omitted list field clears that list. Only these keys are accepted — anything else is a 400. networkOff (EGRESS_POLICY_ENABLED deployments) is the one-call deny-all: true becomes denyOut ["0.0.0.0/0"] gateway-side (an explicit denyOut in the same body wins; combined with allowOut that is the allowlist pattern) and the key itself is never forwarded; false is consumed with no effect, and any non-boolean value (null included) is a 400

allowOut.description: CIDRs, bare IPs, domains (`*.example.com`) or the presets `@packages`/`@trusted`; presets expand gateway-side and the <=64-entry cap applies after expansion. Entries are canonicalised (hosts lowercased, trailing dot stripped; IPv4-mapped IPv6 must be written as IPv4) and must be public targets — loopback, link-local, RFC1918, CGNAT, multicast, reserved/unspecified ranges, local zones and numeric-host IP spellings are a 400, and the wide forms `*`, `0.0.0.0/0`, `::/0` need the node's ALLOW_TENANT_WIDE_EGRESS flag. Entries are capped at 253 BYTES (not characters) and must be valid UTF-8

denyOut.description: CIDRs/IPs/domains — presets are not valid here; entries are canonicalised like allowOut, and since a deny can only narrow egress, private targets and a `/0` deny-all stay valid; entries capped at 253 bytes

networkOff.description: true = turn this sandbox's egress off: translated to the canonical denyOut ["0.0.0.0/0"] before the hop, so the upstream only ever sees the lists

NewSandbox.description: E2B v1 create body; unlisted fields pass through to the upstream untouched. cpuCount/memoryMB/resourceClass follow the take-effect-or-400 sizing contract (a SIZED_TEMPLATES variant applies the size; anything else is a 400 unless UPSTREAM_HONORS_CREATE_SIZING), diskSizeMB the node's disk cap, timeout SANDBOX_MAX_TIMEOUT_S, and network.allowOut/denyOut are validated and canonicalised before forwarding. Under EGRESS_POLICY_ENABLED the network block may also carry networkOff (translated to the canonical deny-all), and an explicit allow_internet_access: true beside that deny-all is a 400 — the pair has no single meaning

autoPause.description: consumed by the gateway: picks the idle reaper's action when the keep-alive lapses — true/omitted -> paused (never before the IDLE_PAUSE_SECONDS idle floor, default 300 s, and up to a reaper sweep late), false -> killed (E2B's lifecycle.onTimeout=kill)

autoResume.description: data-plane auto-resume of a paused sandbox (default false — connect always resumes); true (or {"enabled": true}) lets data-plane traffic wake it

cpuCount.description: vCPUs; applied only as a cpuCount+memoryMB pair equal to a class spec — mapped to the template's SIZED_TEMPLATES variant, else a 400 (forwarded bounded by TEMPLATE_MAX_CPU only when the deployment's upstream honors per-create sizing)

info.description:
E2B-compatible multi-tenant front door for agent sandboxes. Point the stock e2b SDKs at it with E2B_DOMAIN=<domain> and E2B_API_KEY=<tenant key>; the gateway owns API keys, per-key quotas, sandbox tenancy, lifecycle metering and idle auto-pause.

Auth: every tenant route takes the tenant API key in the `X-API-Key` header (the e2b SDK sends it from E2B_API_KEY). /healthz, /v1/waitlist, /v1/claim, /v1/tiers, the GitHub signup redirects and the discovery docs (/openapi.json, /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt) are unauthenticated.

Errors use the E2B wire envelope {"code": <http status>, "message": "..."} with an optional machine-readable `error_code`; 429s that are safe to retry carry an integer `Retry-After` header.

This document covers the public tenant API only; routes outside it are not part of the E2B-compatible surface.

Answers 201 with the registration. The url is validated (SSRF guard): https only on port 443 and it must resolve only to public unicast addresses (loopback, the 169.254.169.254 metadata service, RFC1918/CGNAT private and the IPv6 ULA range fc00::/7 are refused 400; a resolve slower than 5 s is refused 400 too). post.description: Server-mints a new whsec_-style signing secret and returns it once, in signatureSecret. The replaced secret stays accepted for a grace window (WEBHOOK_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS, default 300s): deliveries dual-sign x-agent-next-signature 'v1=<new>,v1=<prev>' until it closes, so receivers should accept either token while they update their stored secret. The grace window covers only x-agent-next-signature — the legacy e2b-signature is a single value signed with the active secret and is never dual-signed, so migrate a legacy receiver to x-agent-next-signature BEFORE rotating. PATCH signatureSecret also replaces the secret but takes effect immediately with no grace.

get.description: Proxied to the upstream, then intersected with the caller's owned set — another tenant's row can never appear. `envdAccessToken`/`trafficAccessToken` are stripped from every item (bulk surfaces carry no credentials). `state` is coerced into the SDK enum (running|paused) and `domain` rewritten to the gateway domain. The tenant-visible list is paginated gateway-side in deterministic (created_at, sandboxID) order: `order` (default desc), `limit` 1-100 (default 100) and the `nextToken` continuation cursor are enforced on both dialects; any upstream pagination headers are stripped and the gateway's own X-Next-Token / X-Total-Running are emitted instead. `metadata` filters the result (url-encoded k=v pairs, AND-ed against the stored create metadata) so a tenant can list what it owns; per-item `metadata` is filled from the stored copy when the upstream echo omits it, and `PUT /sandboxes/{sandbox_id}/metadata` merges lifecycle tags (kept_reason) into that stored copy.

parameters.description: url-encoded k=v pairs (metadata=owner_lane%3Dlane-a); every pair must match the stored create metadata — list what you own
parameters.name: metadata

X-Next-Token.description: present only when more pages remain; pass back verbatim as `nextToken` (opaque HMAC-signed cursor, bound to the tenant and the order direction)

X-Total-Running.description: the tenant's total running sandbox count; present because no `state` filter excluded running

get.summary: List the calling tenant's sandboxes

post.description: Passes auth, per-tenant running-quota (429 + Retry-After), credit (402), suspension (403), create-rate (429 + Retry-After) and node-capacity/host-disk admission (503 + Retry-After) gates, then forwards upstream. `templateID` resolves per tenant: own alias/id, a platform template, an owned snapshot id, or 404; omitted/`base` maps to the deployment's default template when one is configured. An omitted `timeout` defaults to 300 s, capped by SANDBOX_MAX_TIMEOUT_S; an omitted `secure` is injected `true` on secure-capable upstreams unless the deployment disabled it. A size request must take effect or fail (#427): `resourceClass` — or a `cpuCount`/`memoryMB` pair exactly matching a class spec — rewrites `templateID` to the template's SIZED_TEMPLATES variant and drops the sizing fields; a class with no variant for that template is a 400 naming the classes it does have, and any other raw pair is a 400 — unless the deployment set UPSTREAM_HONORS_CREATE_SIZING, which forwards raw values bounded by the node's template caps. SDK users cannot send `resourceClass`, so a `templateID` of the form `<alias>:<size>` (`agent-full:standard`) is the same request in the SDK dialect: it resolves to the variant that class would pick, is refused (disabled class 400, unknown size 404 naming the sizes that alias does offer, a disagreeing `resourceClass` 400) exactly as the field is, and is advertised by GET /templates; a ref that resolves on its own (a tenant's `name:tag` alias, a template id, an owned snapshot id) keeps resolving verbatim. A tenant's own template keeps its built size (a matching request is a no-op); a snapshot id never maps. The response reports the applied spec's `cpuCount`/`memoryMB` — the variant's upstream templateID never leaves the gateway. `diskSizeMB` stays bounded by the node's disk cap.

post.description: The e2b SDK's connect path. On a paused sandbox this is a start: the same capacity/disk admission, running-quota and credit gates as resume apply. On a running sandbox the upstream call is serialized with the other token writers and the response carries the current `envdAccessToken`. The request body is optional: a missing body or non-JSON Content-Type is accepted and an omitted `timeout` defaults to the sandbox's stored keep-alive (the create/resume timeout, 300 s by default). An unknown or killed id answers 404 'sandbox <id> not found'.

put.description: Available only when the local accel plane or GPU node mode is enabled, for owned gl-* leases with container-backed public execution. A GPU lease has no network unless it was created with accel.network "internet". Streams the raw body in chunks, creates parent directories inside OUTPUT_DIR, and atomically replaces the file after completion. The name is relative to the job's OUTPUT_DIR (<workdir>/out): the job reads it there, and GET /sandboxes/{id}/files[/{name}] lists and downloads it back. Same path validation as GPU downloads: no absolute paths, empty/dot/dot-dot components, backslashes, NUL, components over 255 characters, names over 1024 characters, or more than five components. Symlinked roots, parents and existing destinations are refused. Both front and node enforce GATEWAY_GPU_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES (default 512 MiB) on actual streamed bytes, regardless of Content-Length. Paused, frozen or transitioning leases return 409 without resuming; dead, unknown and foreign leases return 404. Leases have no dedicated disk quota; disk-write failure returns 507.

parameters.description: Workdir-relative file path; nested components may be separated by /.
parameters.name: name

404.description: Unknown, foreign or dead lease, or unsafe file path

413.description: Upload exceeds the front or node byte cap

502.description: Invalid or interrupted node upload receipt

503.description: Node unreachable or node build lacks file uploads

post.description: Each fork is a new sandbox passing the create gate (running quota 429, credit 402, create rate limit) and recorded as the tenant's own. The upstream forks one sandbox per call, so `count` fans out into per-fork upstream calls; a first-fork upstream refusal is the whole request's answer. A paused source forks from its pause checkpoint: the upstream refuses to fork or snapshot a paused sandbox, so the gateway resumes it, snapshots it, pauses it again and creates from that snapshot behind the same call (`count` honored; the source ends paused under its original pause label but runs, and is metered, for the checkpoint, and needs a free running-sandbox slot like a resume). When the checkpoint cannot be taken it is a 409 and the source is paused again.

201.description: one entry per requested fork — `sandbox` on success, `error` once the per-fork pipeline failed (later forks share the verdict)

X-Sandbox-Timeout-Applied.description: present only for a key with a max_timeout_s cap: the keep-alive seconds applied to this request after clamping to min(SANDBOX_MAX_TIMEOUT_S, the key's cap)

post.summary: Fork a sandbox into N clones (E2B v4 shape)

put.description: Our extension beyond the E2B wire: merges the body's tags into the metadata stored at create (the create copy is kept, the merge never replaces). The stored copy is the list `?metadata=` filter's authority, so a merge is visible to filtered lists immediately. Gateway-local state: no upstream call, so a paused sandbox is tagged the same as a running one. Answers 200 with the merged metadata. A non-object body, a body carrying the reserved `__gwIdemOp` key, or a merge that would push the stored metadata past 16 KiB is a 400 (refused, never truncated).

schema.description: tags to merge into the stored metadata (free-form keys, JSON-safe values)

put.summary: Merge lifecycle tags into a sandbox's stored metadata

get.description: Available only when the deployment enables EGRESS_POLICY_ENABLED (absent otherwise — the path then falls through to the generic sandbox subpath proxy). Gateway-local: the gateway answers from the allowOut/denyOut lists it stored at create time and on PUT network — no upstream call, so a paused sandbox answers too, and an out-of-band upstream mutation could diverge from this view (source says whose it is). No stored policy answers `{}` — no stored policy, not a promise of open: an explicit `allow_internet_access: false` (or its camelCase twin on the v2 create and fork dialects, which document it) stores the deny-all it means, but the camelCase spelling on the v1 create dialect is not that dialect's field — forwarded verbatim, ignored upstream, stored as nothing.
get.summary: Read back the sandbox's stored egress policy

post.description: E2B's update_network route; the beta does not ship it, so it answers a clear 501 (after auth) instead of a 404/405.

put.description: Our extension beyond the E2B wire (AgentENV deployments; an nvx upstream answers 405): the upstream replaces the sandbox's egress rules with the body's `allowOut`/`denyOut` lists — omitting a field clears it, so `{}` reopens all egress. `allowOut` entries are CIDRs, bare IPs, domains (`*.example.com`) or the presets `@packages` (language/OS package + container registries) and `@trusted` (@packages + git hosts, the Hugging Face hub, big-three cloud SDK endpoints, the gateway's own API/MCP hosts): the gateway expands presets into concrete host lists before the hop, an unknown `@name` answers 400, and the <=64-entry/<=253-byte caps are checked after expansion. A paused sandbox answers 409; the response is the upstream's.
put.summary: Replace a running sandbox's egress rules

post.description: Draws a pause slot, re-checks state under the sandbox lock, enforces the per-tenant paused quota (429 `quota_paused_exceeded` + Retry-After 5), then forwards upstream. Re-asserting pause on an already-paused sandbox marks it user-paused; whether data-plane traffic wakes it is the create's `autoResume` (default false — 502 not-found; `connect` always resumes).

get.description: Every registered port of this sandbox, sorted by port (our extension beyond the E2B wire). Each entry carries the port's `public` flag, `title`, access `token` (HMAC-derived per sandbox+port — the row itself never stores credential material) and the data-plane `url` it unlocks. A port only appears here after PUT /sandboxes/{id}/ports/{port}: non-envd ports serve open by default (E2B parity) — a `public:false` row is what engages the token gate.
get.summary: List the sandbox's data-plane port registry

put.description: Our extension beyond the E2B wire: registers (or updates) the port's `public` flag and optional `title`. Non-envd ports serve open by default — E2B parity, `network.allowPublicTraffic` defaults true — so `public:false` is the opt-in that engages the gate: the port's <port>-<sandbox_id>.<domain> URL then answers 401 without a credential (the port's `token` as `?_gw_token=<token>` or `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or the sandbox's `trafficAccessToken` as the E2B `e2b-traffic-access-token` header; a recognized gateway credential is consumed on every non-envd forward, open port or gated). A sandbox created with `network.allowPublicTraffic=false` is gated on EVERY non-envd port regardless of this flag. The response carries the derived `token` and the `url`; the token is HMAC-derived, never stored. The envd port (its own fixed token gate) and out-of-range port values answer 400. Gateway-local metadata: no upstream call, so a paused sandbox's registry still updates.
put.summary: Set a data-plane port's public flag and title

post.description: Runs agent-prompt <harness> -- <task> inside the sandbox via the envd data plane; envs apply to that run only and are never stored. Start-gated like create (402 credit, 403 suspended, 429 rate / live-prompt cap); done requires an observed exit 0. Observe with GET /sandboxes/{sandbox_id}/events.

post.description: A resume adds a running sandbox: suspended (403), abuse-paused (403), quota (429), credit (402) and the capacity/disk admission gates (503 + Retry-After) all apply. An empty body is accepted (E2B shape): the sandbox timeout is filled in, invalid JSON answers 400. An upstream 409 'already running' is reconciled to a 200-class answer, not an error. The response carries the current `envdAccessToken`.

get.description: Served from the gateway's own snapshot records (the upstream list cannot filter per org), so a snapshot created out-of-band upstream is invisible here. Items carry a `status` (pending/ready/failed) — the poll surface for an async create (#420). `name`/`limit` (1-100, default 100) filter the set; `nextToken` is not implemented on this route and no `x-next-token` is emitted.

get.summary: List this sandbox's snapshots (tenant-owned records)

post.description: Snapshotting is incremental upstream (~9 s/GB), so the create does not ride one long request: the gateway records a pending snapshot under a minted id and runs the upstream call on its own budget. Within a short inline window the finished answer is relayed (201, the snapshot object); past it the answer is still 201 with the pending snapshot and `status: "pending"` — 201 is what the e2b SDK's create_snapshot parses, and pending-then-poll is E2B's own async build pattern. Poll the GET lists for `status` `ready`/`failed` (the SDK's SnapshotInfo drops the field — an SDK client probes readiness by attempting the restore, which 409s while pending); a `pending` snapshot is not yet a valid `templateID` (409). The snapshot id is recorded against the calling tenant because the upstream list has no per-org filter. A paused source is left to the upstream to decide, except an abuse-paused one (403).

201.description: the new snapshot — ready when the inline window covered the create, `status: "pending"` otherwise (poll the lists)

429.description: too many snapshots already pending for this key (Retry-After)

post.description: Creates a Stripe Checkout Session in setup mode (no charge) for the calling key and returns its URL. After the signed webhook confirms the card the key moves to the verified tier: the credit difference is added once and concurrency rises. One card fingerprint upgrades at most one account.

post.description: Once an operator approved the signup, the first claim mints the key and returns the secret exactly once (`issued`); later claims answer `claimed` with the key id only. Pending/rejected signups answer 200 with their status. Unknown tokens also answer 200 {"status": "pending"}, identical to an unapproved claim, so repeat signup tokens do not disclose whether an email is stored. The body may be form-encoded (`curl -d claim_token=...`); the answer is always JSON.

post.description: Authenticated by the current key. The tenant keeps its credit, usage, sandboxes, snapshots and webhooks; the old secret stops working in the same commit and the new one is returned once. A second rotation with the already-replaced key answers 401. Browser-callable from SITE_ORIGIN.

A GitHub id that already claimed its key is redirected with `#signup=exists`.

post.description: Per-client-IP rate-limited (429) and body-capped (413). The 202 is identical for a new and an already-stored email — it never reveals whether an address is known — but its `claim_token` only redeems for the first signup of an address; only the token's sha256 is stored. The body may also be form-encoded (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, e.g. `curl -d email=...` or a plain HTML form post, no JavaScript needed); a form post that sends `Accept: text/html` (a browser) gets a self-contained HTML page with the claim token and the claim command instead of JSON, for the 202 and for the 400/413/429 refusals.

On a v2-capable upstream those params are relayed and the upstream validates, but `limit` and `nextToken` are always the gateway's own (none of the proxied upstreams paginate).

post.description: The same auth/quota/admission/metering pipeline as POST /sandboxes. Forwarded verbatim to a v2-capable upstream; on a v1-only upstream it is translated to the v1 create and fields the v1 upstream cannot express are refused with 400 naming them: `network`, `mcp`, `iam`, `volumeMounts`, unknown fields, non-boolean `autoPause`/`secure`/`autoPauseMemory`, `autoPauseMemory: false`, a malformed `autoResume`. Both `allow_internet_access` and `allowInternetAccess` are accepted inbound; an explicit internet allow paired with the canonical deny-all network block (`networkOff: true`-equivalent) is a 400 under EGRESS_POLICY_ENABLED — the pair has no single meaning. `cpuCount`/`memoryMB`/`resourceClass` follow the same take-effect-or-400 sizing contract as POST /sandboxes (a SIZED_TEMPLATES variant applies the size; otherwise a 400) — including the `<alias>:<size>` templateID ref.
